samples.summary: `--dry-run` early-returns before the new `parseOutputFormat()` guard, so `--format bogus --dry-run` is still silently accepted
samples.evidence: In `cells set` the dry-run branch runs at cells.ts:52-60 and `return`s before the `try` block where `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` is called (cells.ts:63). Same shape at cells.ts:86 (`delete`), cells.ts:129 (`batch`), docs.ts:135/154 (`update`/`delete`), notes.ts:94/113, slides.ts:99/118. The stated invariant of the change is that "an unsupported format fails loudly instead of being ignored" (formatter.ts:24-34) and that validation happens "before doing any work", but the whole dry-run path reaches its `printDryRun` output with the flag unvalidated. Result: `wafflebase sheets cells set d A1 v --format bogus --dry-run` exits 0, while the identical command without `--dry-run` exits 1 with INVALID_FORMAT — the exact inconsistency the guard was added to remove. (Note `docs create`/`notes create`/`slides create` do validate first, so the treatment is not even uniform inside the same change.)

samples.summary: New `cell()` JSON-serialization is applied only to the single-object path; the array path still prints `[object Object]`
samples.evidence: `cell()` (table.ts:7-10) is documented as fixing nested values that "would print `[object Object]`", but it is only used by `formatRecord` (table.ts:24). The array branch still computes widths with `String(row[key] ?? '')` (table.ts:46) and renders with `String(row[k] ?? '')` (table.ts:53). So any list-shaped payload with a nested field — e.g. `sheets cells get <doc> A1:B2 --format table`, `docs list --format table` if a document carries a nested field — still renders `[object Object]`, whereas the same payload wrapped in a single object renders JSON. The new test only covers the record path (`schema ctx.list --format table`), so nothing catches the asymmetry.

samples.summary: `ctx list` changes from exit 0 + prose to exit 1 + JSON error when logged out, breaking any caller that treated "no session" as success
samples.evidence: Previously `ctx list` with no session printed to stdout and returned normally (exit 0). It now throws `NotLoggedInError` (ctx.ts:78) into `outputError`, which sets `process.exitCode = 1` (formatter.ts:87). Any script doing `wafflebase ctx list && ...` or running under `set -e` now aborts where it previously continued. The change is deliberate and documented (docs/design/cli.md:721-722, task doc "Decisions"), so this is flagged only as an unguarded behavioral break for existing callers, not a defect in the implementation. Under `--quiet` the failure is completely silent: exit 1 with no message at all (formatter.ts:79-82).

samples.summary: `NotLoggedInError` hardcodes the message string instead of reusing the exported `NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE`, so the two can drift
samples.evidence: ctx.ts:39 has the literal 'Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.' while status.ts:31 exports `NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE` with the identical text (and ctx.ts:95 has a third copy in `ctx switch`). Nothing keeps them in sync; a future wording change to one leaves the CLI emitting two different messages for the same condition. No test asserts the ctx.ts copies match.

finding.summary: `cells batch` parses `--data`/stdin JSON outside the try block, so malformed input becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of the structured error body the diff's own rationale relies on
finding.evidence: cells.ts:117-127: `cells = JSON.parse(dataStr)` (line 119) and the stdin `JSON.parse` (line 126) sit above the `try` that starts at line 139. In an async commander action a throw here rejects the returned promise; `bin.ts` (line 27, `program.parse()`) installs no rejection handler, so `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc --data '{'` prints a raw stack trace / triggers an unhandled-rejection crash rather than the `{ "error": { ... } }` body §8.1 promises. Pre-existing, but it is the exact failure mode the schema.ts hunk of this change cites ("bin.ts has no top-level handler") and adjacent to the modified try blocks.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is exactly as described. In the `cells batch` action (packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:110-151), `JSON.parse(dataStr)` at line 119 and `JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf-8'))` at line 126 — plus the `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` loop at line 123 — sit above the `try` that begins at line 139, whose catch (lines 148-149) is the only path to `outputError`. The action is async, so a throw there rejects the returned promise. bin.ts:27 calls the synchronous `program.parse()` with no `.catch`, and grep found no `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException`/`process.on(` handler anywhere in packages/cli/src; root.ts:42-59 adds no error hook or exitOverride either. The command is reachable via sheets.ts:15 (`registerCellsCommand(sheets)`), so `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc --data '{'` yields a raw unhandled-rejection stack trace instead of the structured error body every sibling command in the file emits (lines 33, 74, 101, 149). This is error handling that mis-routes a real failure on a real user path — squarely in the correctness lane, and not refutable on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds.
